content.title: Tennyson Knolls Park: Turf Conversion and Park Improvements
content.summary: Tennyson Knolls Park in Arvada is undergoing a turf conversion from bluegrass to native grass as part of the city's Turf Conversion Program, aimed at conserving water and resources. Community feedback gathered during a meeting on November 19, 2025, highlighted concerns about park maintenance, safety, and the use of the new native grass area, which is expected to save over 830,000 gallons of water annually once established. The city plans to continue improvements and reassess the area in three years based on community input.
content.body:
As part of the [City of Arvada's Turf Conversion Program](/1019), a portion of bluegrass at Tennyson Knolls Park is being converted to native grass. This project is part of the City’s ongoing efforts to conserve water and resources while maintaining beautiful, usable parks.

In addition to the turf conversion, the City is planning for both near-term improvements and longer-term, comprehensive upgrades at Tennyson Knolls Park. Community input will play a key role in shaping these efforts.

## Tennyson Knolls Park Community Meeting

The City of Arvada and Arvada Voices hosted a community meeting on Nov. 19, 2025 at Tennyson Knolls Preparatory School to discuss the turf conversion project and gather feedback on future park improvements.

- [View the presentation the City's Parks Department gave during the meeting.](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14K7p1AfOUfNPlfhVplUdGTVt4Ik5btQmTCSeZxKiyvM/edit?usp=sharing)

### Sign up for the project email list to stay updated

[Sign up for the Tennyson Knolls Park email list](https://app.e2ma.net/app2/audience/signup/2043821/1717219/) to receive updates on future community engagement opportunities or when significant milestones are achieved.

### [Email List](https://app.e2ma.net/app2/audience/signup/2043821/1717219/ "Tennyson Knolls Park Email List")

[View an email update from Dec. 10](https://t.e2ma.net/webview/5jmpmr/fca64b2b8f0d85c84000a783d22f6458) that recaps what we heard during the Nov. 19 community meeting.

## What we heard from the community

During the meeting and small group discussions, several consistent themes emerged:

- **Park maintenance**: Community members shared concerns about the condition of remaining bluegrass areas. The City acknowledges that maintenance fell below expectations earlier in 2025 and has taken steps to restore and maintain park conditions going forward.
- **Active recreation space**: Families emphasized the importance of informal play and open space. More than 7 acres of irrigated bluegrass will remain available throughout the park.
- **Safety and accessibility**: Lighting, visibility, and overall safety were raised as important considerations and will be addressed as part of future park planning.
- **Use of the native grass area**: Residents shared ideas to make the converted area more welcoming, including soft trails, native flowers, pollinator habitat, and educational elements.
- **Communication**: The City recognizes that earlier engagement would have been beneficial and is committed to improving communication moving forward.

### Turf conversion moving forward

The turf conversion at Tennyson Knolls Park will continue as planned. This area was selected due to long-standing challenges with poor soil conditions and an outdated irrigation system with limited coverage.

Once fully established, the native grass area is expected to save more than 830,000 gallons of water each year. The area was overseeded in the fall of 2025 and native grass establishment will continue over the next several years.

In approximately three years, the City will reevaluate the converted area and gather community feedback to assess how it is functioning.

### Why This Location?

A large section on the north side of Tennyson Knolls Park is being converted from bluegrass to native grass. This location was chosen for the following reasons:

- The area was identified as low-use, meaning it’s rarely used for active or passive recreation.
- The park’s irrigation system is outdated, with poor coverage and an inefficient design.
- Soil conditions consist largely of clay and rock, making bluegrass difficult to maintain.
- The park contains 11.75 irrigated acres, leaving more than 7 acres of irrigated bluegrass remaining for recreation.
- Once established, native grass will reduce long-term costs for mowing, watering, and fertilizer.

![Aerial view of Tennyson Knolls Park, with 3.5 acres of the eastern side of the park highlighted](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6311)

### What Park Users Can Expect

- Some areas may appear dark brown; this is treated bindweed, not dead grass.
- Remaining irrigated bluegrass areas will continue to be maintained as usual.
- Over time, the converted area will transition to a natural, open-space appearance.

## Park Improvements

Based on community feedback, the City is taking action on several near-term improvements:

- Trash receptacles and dog waste stations: Additional trash cans and a limited number of dog waste stations will be installed in spring. (Please note: community members will need to supply their own waste bags.)
- Soft trail through the native grass area: The City is exploring a crushed granite walking trail to improve accessibility and create a more intentional space. Construction is anticipated in fall/winter 2026.
- Bench maintenance: Park benches will be recoated to improve appearance and longevity.
- Playground surfacing repairs: Select playground surfacing will be replaced where repairs are needed.

## Looking Ahead: Comprehensive Park Improvements

Within the next four to five years, the playground at Tennyson Knolls Park will be due for replacement through the [City’s Taking Lasting Care program](/860).

By combining those funds with accumulated Adams County Open Space tax dollars, the City plans to pursue a comprehensive park improvement project, rather than isolated upgrades. This approach allows for:

- Replacement of the aging playground with modern, accessible equipment
- Improved pathways and trail connections
- Strategic upgrades to amenities based on community priorities

Before this project moves forward, additional community engagement will be conducted to ensure resident input shapes the final design.

### Stay connected

The City is committed to keeping neighbors informed as this project progresses. Sign up for the Tennyson Knolls Park email list to receive the latest information about the project.

Have questions or feedback? Contact us through [Ask Arvada](/898).
